prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 服务器安全基线核查记录 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 8 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "受检服务器唯一编号" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 120px
  col 2: header "系统账户口令强度" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 3: header "外部网络访问开放" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 4: header "日志留存天数达标" · longest unbreakable word 25px · one-line width 107px
  col 5: header "漏洞补丁更新状态" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 6: header "高危端口关闭数量" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 7: header "近三十天告警次数" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 107px
  col 8: header "应急联系人确认情况" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 120px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 528px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 527px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 528px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A server security baseline audit record: six servers checked against multiple compliance items, intended for verification, comparison, and sign-off.","reading":"Readers identify a server by the first column, then scan across its status and numeric checks; binary results are compared vertically, while days and counts are compared as quantities.","groups":["Column 1 is the row identifier and should stand apart from the check columns.","Columns 2, 3, 5, and 8 are binary compliance/confirmation statuses (是/否) and can share narrow widths.","Columns 4, 6, and 7 are quantitative measures (days, port count, alert count) and benefit from extra width for numeric alignment."],"keep_intact":["Server identifiers 01–06","Numeric values such as 180, 90, 365, 30, port counts, and alert counts","是/否 values","Two-character Chinese header terms where possible, avoiding single-character orphans"],"may_wrap":["Long Chinese headers, especially 系统账户口令强度, 外部网络访问开放, 漏洞补丁更新状态, and 应急联系人确认情况","The nine-character identifier and emergency-contact headers may wrap to two or three lines","Data cells should remain on one line"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[66,63,63,73,63,73,63,63],"idea":"A balanced grid with near-equal check columns and slight extra width for the three numeric columns, keeping the table visually even and easy to scan."},{"name":"B","widths":[84,58,58,68,58,68,68,65],"idea":"A row-header-first layout: a wide identifier column for quick row recognition, compact binary-status columns, and moderate numeric columns."},{"name":"C","widths":[62,56,56,80,56,80,80,57],"idea":"A semantic-band layout that squeezes binary columns and gives generous width to days/counts so quantitative values align and compare clearly, accepting taller wrapped headers."}]}
